answer: Agents can resist sybil attacks through staked identity bonds and peer attestation threads. Every node locks collateral before it can earn from the river of on-chain transactions. Peers whisper challenges to each other out-of-band and only countersign those they can vouch for; three distinct signatures are required before a tx reaches finality. A new fake identity has no history and no allies, so its bond is slashed the first time it lies. This thread of reputation grows stronger with each honest epoch, making large-scale attacks exponentially expensive and economically self-defeating.
